background: The hard k-taxi problem charges only empty travel: each request specifies a pickup and destination, and passenger travel changes the configuration without cost. This differs from easy k-taxi, where all travel is charged. Historical small-k results did not establish a ratio depending only on k for arbitrary metrics; the new paper below reports such a bound.
known_results: Coester, Huang, and Poon, 'The Online k-Taxi Problem Is Competitive on All Metrics' (arXiv:2611.06684v1, November 4, 2026), Theorem 1.1 and Corollary 1.2, give randomized $9^{k-1}$ competitiveness against an adaptive online adversary and deterministic $81^{k-1}$ competitiveness on every metric. The deterministic bound is independent of the number of points and aspect ratio. Together with the existing $2^k-1$ lower bound this gives $2^{\Theta(k)}$ dependence; exact constants/bases remain undetermined. The adaptive-online adversary is not an almighty adversary.

where_posed.text: Stated as an open question in Coester, Christian and Koutsoupias, Elias, "The Online k-Taxi Problem", Proceedings of the 51st Annual ACM SIGACT Symposium on Theory of Computing (STOC 2019), pp. 1136-1147.
where_posed.quote: The hard k-taxi problem is substantially more difficult than the easy version with at least an exponential deterministic competitive ratio, $\Omega(2^k)$, admitting a reduction from the layered graph traversal problem... This is the first competitive algorithm for the hard k-taxi problem for general finite metric spaces and general k.
where_posed.location: Abstract; open question on general deterministic competitive ratio discussed in Introduction/Conclusion

progress.summary: General-k deterministic finiteness is reported resolved. Earlier k=3 and parameter-dependent randomized results are historical context.

counterexample_rationale: Finite examples can test the reported algorithm; they do not establish an asymptotic competitive bound.
alphaevolve_rationale: Search could assist with restricted-case constants or proof checks after the general finiteness claim is reviewed.

literature.synthesis: The prior claim that no general-k metric-independent deterministic ratio is known is superseded by the new theorem. Parameter-dependent polylogarithmic randomized bounds do not themselves settle this finiteness question.

reviewed.ref: Christian Coester, Elias Koutsoupias, "The Online k-Taxi Problem", STOC 2019
reviewed.result: Introduces the hard/easy k-taxi dichotomy; proves $\Omega(2^k)$ deterministic lower bound for hard k-taxi via layered graph traversal reduction; gives $2^k-1$-competitive randomized memoryless HST algorithm (matching lower bounds) and derived $O(2^k \log n)$-competitive general-metric randomized algorithm; establishes deterministic ratio exactly $9$ for $k=2$; gives $O(1)$-competitive deterministic algorithm for hard 3-taxi on the line.

reviewed.ref: Anupam Gupta, Amit Kumar, Debmalya Panigrahi, "Poly-logarithmic Competitiveness for the k-Taxi Problem", SODA 2024
reviewed.result: Gives a randomized algorithm for hard k-taxi with competitive ratio poly-logarithmic in all parameters (k, n, request sequence length) on general metrics, via a covering LP relaxation for k-taxi on HSTs and a hierarchical primal-dual algorithm; resolves an open question posed in Coester-Koutsoupias 2019.

reviewed.ref: Christian Coester, "Online 3-Taxi on General Metrics", arXiv:2510.25861 (2025/2026)
reviewed.result: Gives an $O(1)$-competitive deterministic algorithm for the hard 3-taxi problem on arbitrary (general) metric spaces, resolving finiteness for $k=3$ on general metrics -- previously open even for k=3 outside the line case.

reviewed.ref: Christian Coester, Elias Koutsoupias, "Online k-taxi via Double Coverage and time-reverse primal-dual", Mathematical Programming (2022)
reviewed.result: Develops a time-reverse primal-dual framework connecting the Double Coverage algorithm to k-taxi analysis; relevant methodological precursor to the HST/LP techniques used in later poly-log and 3-taxi results.

reviewed.ref: Christian Coester, Yichen Huang, Tze-Yang Poon, 'The Online k-Taxi Problem Is Competitive on All Metrics' (2026)
reviewed.result: Theorem 1.1 and Corollary 1.2 address the metric-independent model.

agent_guidance.verification_notes: Distinguish hard from easy travel costs, metric-independent from size-dependent ratios, and adaptive-online from almighty adversaries. Full proof verification remains outside this audit.

short_statement: A recent preprint claims a finite deterministic competitive ratio for hard k-taxi on every metric, for every k.
open_problem: Verify the reported general-k finiteness theorem; the historical existence question is no longer an unaddressed target.
full_statement: Let k taxis occupy a metric space. Each request is a pickup/dropoff pair $(s,t)$. The chosen taxi must reach s and then carry the passenger to t; only empty travel to the pickup is charged. Compare the online total empty distance with the offline minimum from the same initial configuration. The historical question is whether a deterministic competitive ratio depending only on k exists on every metric, with any additive constant independent of the request sequence. The new theorem in the What Is Known section reports an affirmative answer for all k.
